notes: Customer is a mid-market SaaS vendor running a multitenant agent platform for B2B customers
Primary workload: chat-based assistants for support + internal tooling via tool-calls (calendar, CRM queries)
Latency target: 95th pct for streaming tokens < 250ms end-to-end (they repeatedly stated: "users notice stalls")
Throughput: expecting baseline 20k active sessions concurrently across tenants; burst to 80k during peak
Per-tenant quotas desired: soft throttles (grace) + hard caps; billing attribution per tenant + per-feature
Want hosted POC first to validate streaming stability and function-calling reliability; move to Dedicated once SLOs met
Infrastructure: Kubernetes on AWS (EKS), Postgres primary, Redis for session KV. Prefer minimal infra changes if using Hosted API
Security: must be SOC2 compliant; SAML SSO for team access; KMS for key wraps if Dedicated; data residency preference EU for some customers
Quoted on calls: "If streaming drops, customers churn — so reliability > cost savings initially."
Technical ask: SDK to surface per-tenant rate usage and per-request routing metadata (model variant, region, cost estimate)
POC success metric: <5% token drop/reconnect events during 2-week heavy workload; 95th token latency <250ms; no functional-call failures >0.5%
use_case_summary: Mid-market multi-tenant chat/agent SaaS evaluating Redwood Hosted API to validate streaming token latency and tool-calling reliability. After a successful hosted POC they plan to evaluate Dedicated for predictable capacity and lower unit cost. Needs per-tenant quotas and billing attribution, SSO/SAML and SOC2 compliance, and clear fallback behavior when capacity constrained.
